resources.name: TBG conservation grants database
resources.description: The most comprehensive list of wildlife grants anywhere, over 1,100 of them, with an assistant that remembers your mission and programs and ranks which grants actually fit you. Open to Fiscal Sponsorship Alliance members only
resources.use_note: Get over 1,100 wildlife grants ranked against your own mission, as a Fiscal Sponsorship Alliance member

resources.name: Phoenix Species Project
resources.description: Re:wild, the Bezos Earth Fund and IUCN SSC putting $200M into recovering 100 Critically Endangered and Extinct-in-the-Wild species across 30 countries. No open call or application route is published
resources.use_note: See whether your species is among the 100, which decides whether serious money exists

resources.name: Terra Viva Grants Directory
resources.description: Grants for agriculture, energy and environment in developing countries
resources.use_note: Search free listings aimed at developing countries, where most grant databases are weakest

resources.name: fundsforNGOs
resources.description: Grant listings and proposal resources
resources.use_note: Scan frequent calls, but verify each at source since the listings are aggregated

resources.name: Foundation Directory Online
resources.description: Candid funder database, paywalled
resources.use_note: Reach it through a library or partner if you cannot justify the subscription yourself

resources.name: Candid Learning
resources.description: Candid's free training and knowledge base on funding, formerly GrantSpace
resources.use_note: Take the free training, and search GrantSpace for anything you remember under the old name

resources.name: Peak Proposals free grant search list
resources.description: Guide to free grant-funding search sources
resources.use_note: Start here with no budget, because it lists the genuinely free search sources first

resources.name: Unfunded List
resources.description: Feedback on unfunded proposals
resources.use_note: Send a rejected proposal for outside evaluation before resubmitting it unchanged

resources.name: Conservation Leadership Programme
resources.description: Early-career conservation team grants
resources.use_note: Apply as an early-career team, which is rare when most funders will only fund institutions

resources.name: Mohamed bin Zayed Species Conservation Fund
resources.description: Species grants with a public grant database
resources.use_note: Search past grants to see the realistic size and shape of an award before applying

resources.name: CEPF
resources.description: Hotspot grants with public grantee lists
resources.use_note: Check whether your hotspot has an open call, and read the grantee list for local partners

resources.name: Jana Robeyst Trust Fund
resources.description: Small grants for African conservation
resources.use_note: Look for small African conservation grants, confirming the site loads before planning around it

resources.name: Fondation Ensemble
resources.description: French foundation funding biodiversity
resources.use_note: Apply in French for biodiversity funding, which cuts the competition considerably

resources.name: Environmental Funders Network
resources.description: UK environmental philanthropy resources
resources.use_note: Read its fundraiser handbook, and learn who actually funds environmental work in the UK

resources.name: United Philanthropy Forum
resources.description: US philanthropy association network
resources.use_note: Find the regional US philanthropy association nearest you, which knows local funders best

resources.name: Grants.gov
resources.description: US federal grants
resources.use_note: Check eligibility first, since federal registration takes longer than most deadlines allow

resources.name: Instrumentl
resources.description: Grant discovery platform, paid
resources.use_note: Trial it against your real programs, and note the search limits before committing to a subscription

resources.name: GrantScape
resources.description: Grant discovery
resources.use_note: Compare it against other paid platforms rather than assuming coverage differs much

resources.name: Coefficient Giving
resources.description: Grant listings of a major funder, renamed from Open Philanthropy
resources.use_note: Read its published grants for the scale it funds at, and search Open Philanthropy for older history

resources.name: Grantable
resources.description: Funder prospecting with fit scoring, alongside AI proposal drafting built from your own past submissions. Free tier, then $25 a month for nonprofits under $500k
resources.use_note: Draft from your own past proposals rather than a blank page, then check the fit scores

resources.name: NFWF Grants Library
resources.description: Searchable record of the grants the National Fish and Wildlife Foundation has awarded across the United States, with grantee, location, amount and program
resources.use_note: Read what it has funded near you before you pitch, so your request matches the projects and sizes it actually backs

resources.name: GEF Project Database
resources.description: The projects the Global Environment Facility has funded, filterable by country, focal area and agency, with grant amounts and a CSV export
resources.use_note: Check which agencies run projects in your country, since they are the partners you would go through to reach the money

resources.name: GrantNav
resources.description: Search and download grants published by UK funders, by funder, recipient or keyword
resources.use_note: Search your conservation terms to see which UK funders back work like yours and how large their awards run

resources.name: FIRE
resources.description: A database of funding opportunities for biodiversity conservation from around the world, public and private, filterable by country, ecosystem, organization type and amount
resources.use_note: Filter by your country and organization type to find grants, loans and guarantees that the usual grant lists leave out

resources.name: Ramsar funding organizations directory
resources.description: Directory of public and private organizations that fund wetland conservation, wise use and restoration, filterable by region, type and grant size
resources.use_note: Use the grant size filter to match funders to your budget, and email the Secretariat to add one it is missing

resources.name: LIFE Programme project database
resources.description: Search the projects funded by the EU LIFE Programme, with project documents, to see what the European Union supports in nature and biodiversity
resources.use_note: Read the funded projects closest to yours before applying, because their documents show the budgets and results LIFE accepted

resources.name: USAspending.gov
resources.description: The US government's open record of federal grants and contracts, searchable by recipient, agency, program and place
resources.use_note: Look up federal awards to peer organizations in your area to see which programs actually pay for conservation work

resources.name: GlobalGiving
resources.description: Crowdfunding for vetted projects worldwide
resources.use_note: Get vetted once then run repeat campaigns, which suits an organization with no fundraising staff

resources.name: Milkywire
resources.description: Corporate impact firm whose Climate Transformation Fund runs an annual open call, grants averaging $150k to $250k
resources.use_note: Watch for the Climate Transformation Fund open call, where grants run well into six figures

resources.name: Conserve Now
resources.description: Giving federation that pools donations across certified conservation charities, so a small member gets in front of donors who would never find it alone
resources.use_note: Join the federation so payroll donors can reach you without ever hearing your name first

resources.name: Key Conservation
resources.description: App that puts a live campaign in front of supporters when a project needs money now
resources.use_note: Post an urgent need and let supporters fund it live, rather than waiting for a grant cycle

resources.name: Experiment.com
resources.description: Crowdfunding for scientific research
resources.use_note: Crowdfund a specific study when the sum is too small for any foundation to bother with

resources.name: JustGiving
resources.description: Fundraising platform for individual supporters running their own appeals
resources.use_note: Let a supporter run their own appeal, picking up Gift Aid if they are in the UK

resources.name: BiddingForGood
resources.description: Charity auction platform
resources.use_note: Run an online auction when you have donated experiences rather than cash to sell

resources.name: Omaze
resources.description: Prize-draw fundraising
resources.use_note: Understand the prize-draw model before agreeing to be a beneficiary, because the split matters

resources.name: 1% for the Planet
resources.description: Businesses pledge one percent of sales, not profits, to environmental groups. Join as a nonprofit partner to be findable by those members
resources.use_note: Register as a nonprofit partner so member businesses can find you when allocating their pledge

resources.name: Earth Gives
resources.description: A giving day built for environmental organizations, with campaign materials to run your own appeal alongside it
resources.use_note: Time an appeal to the giving day and reuse its materials instead of designing your own

resources.name: TBG shop
resources.description: Conservation merchandise whose proceeds fund the fieldwork, run on Etsy as Aall Forms of Life
resources.use_note: Buy something that funds fieldwork, or copy the model of running a shop through Etsy

resources.name: Gorilla Conservation Coffee
resources.description: Ugandan Arabica grown by farmers living around Bwindi, sold to fund gorilla conservation. The US store, $18 a bag in beans or ground
resources.use_note: Send coffee to a donor as a thank-you gift that also funds gorilla work

resources.name: Global Conservation Force store
resources.description: Apparel, pins, stickers and adoption kits from an anti-poaching group, funding its own work on rhinos, elephants, pangolins and painted dogs
resources.use_note: Buy an adoption kit or apparel when a supporter wants something physical for their money

resources.name: Whitley Awards
resources.description: £50,000 each to six conservation leaders working in their own country. You do not need to be nominated, you apply
resources.use_note: Apply directly with no nomination needed, which is unusual for an award of this size

resources.name: Future For Nature Award
resources.description: €50,000 each to three young conservationists. Open application
resources.use_note: Apply if you are between 18 and 35, since the age band is the real filter

resources.name: St Andrews Prize for the Environment
resources.description: $95,000 to the winner and $20,000 to each runner-up. You enter yourself, no nomination, as an individual, an organization or a community group. Entrants must also be able to host a University of St Andrews student for a two-week internship
resources.use_note: Enter as a group rather than an individual, which most prizes at this level disallow

resources.name: Rolex Awards
resources.description: Five laureates a year across environment, science and exploration. Laureates come from applications, but no open call or eligibility page is published between cycles
resources.use_note: Watch for the next call, because the site gives no date and nothing to apply to in between

resources.name: Explorers Club grants
resources.description: Six named grant programs with live deadlines, from $1,500 to $10,000, plus rolling Impact Grants. Open application, and each program sets its own deadline and career stage
resources.use_note: Match your project to one of six named programs, or use rolling Impact Grants when timing slips

resources.name: WILDLABS Awards
resources.description: $350,000 across up to 15 conservation-tech projects in 2026, at $10,000 and $50,000. Anyone can submit the first-stage expression of interest, and full applications are then invitation only
resources.use_note: Send a first-stage expression of interest, which anyone can do without an invitation

resources.name: National Geographic Society grants and Wayfinder Award
resources.description: Grants run as specific requests for proposals rather than one general open call, and every application goes through the National Geographic funding portal. The Wayfinder Award is by selection, not application
resources.use_note: Match your project to an active request for proposals, because eligibility and deadlines vary by opportunity

resources.name: Goldman Environmental Prize
resources.description: A prize for six grassroots environmental leaders a year, one per world region. Closed to unsolicited nominations
resources.use_note: Do not spend time here unless a nominating partner has already approached you

resources.name: Indianapolis Prize
resources.description: $300,000 biennially, nomination only, but the Emerging Conservationist award for under-40s takes direct applications
resources.use_note: Aim at the Emerging Conservationist award if under 40, since the main prize is nomination only

resources.name: Tyler Prize for Environmental Achievement
resources.description: $250,000, nomination only. The 2026 laureate won it for work on mycorrhizal fungi
resources.use_note: Nominate someone else rather than yourself, and note that nominations close well ahead

resources.name: Blue Planet Prize
resources.description: Two laureates a year, each receiving a trophy, a certificate of merit and a supplementary award of $500,000. Nominated by designated nominators
resources.use_note: Get a designated nominator to put you forward, which means building that relationship first

resources.name: Earthshot Prize
resources.description: £1,000,000 to each of five winners, one being Protect and Restore Nature. Nominated through official nominator organizations, several of which run public expressions of interest
resources.use_note: Watch which nominator organizations run public calls, since that is the only open door

resources.name: Tusk Conservation Awards
resources.description: £225,000 across three awards including a ranger award, paid to the winner's organization over three years. Africa only
resources.use_note: Nominate an African colleague, a ranger included, with the money going to their organization

resources.name: UNESCO Sultan Qaboos Prize
resources.description: $100,000 for environmental conservation. Nominated by governments or NGOs in official relations with UNESCO, no self-nomination
resources.use_note: Ask a government or a UNESCO-linked NGO to nominate you, because self-nomination is refused

resources.name: MIDORI Prize for Biodiversity
resources.description: Biennial biodiversity prize run with the CBD Secretariat, and nominations come in through the website
resources.use_note: Submit through the website in a nomination year, run jointly with the CBD Secretariat

resources.name: Seacology Prize
resources.description: $10,000 to an islander for preserving island environments and culture. The nomination route is not published, so ask them
resources.use_note: Contact them directly about nominating an islander, since the route is not published anywhere

resources.name: Ashden Awards
resources.description: Five awards a year, mostly clean energy, but the Tropical Forest Protection category is a real fit. Judges work from entries you submit yourself, and no 2027 call is open yet
resources.use_note: Watch the Tropical Forest Protection category, which is the one that fits conservation work

resources.name: Disney Conservation Hero Awards
resources.description: $1,000 per hero. Only nominable by nonprofits Disney already funds, so useful if you are one and not otherwise
resources.use_note: Skip it unless Disney already funds you, because nobody else is allowed to nominate

resources.name: Xerces Deborah BanDrosky Award
resources.description: Student research award of about $5,000 for any declining invertebrate, from fireflies to freshwater mollusks. New in 2026, applications open each November
resources.use_note: Point a student at it each November, since almost nothing else funds declining invertebrates broadly

resources.name: Xerces Joan Mosenthal DeWind Award
resources.description: Two student awards a year of about $5,000 for Lepidoptera conservation. Applications open each November
resources.use_note: Send Lepidoptera students here, where two awards a year makes the odds unusually good

resources.name: Royal Entomological Society Insect Conservation Award
resources.description: £400 for insect and invertebrate conservation, and self-nomination is accepted. The live successor to the discontinued Marsh insect award
resources.use_note: Nominate yourself, which is rare, and treat it as successor to the old Marsh insect award

resources.name: Behler Turtle Conservation Award
resources.description: $5,000, treated as the top award in turtle and tortoise conservation. Nominated by specialist group members
resources.use_note: Ask a specialist group member to nominate you, since that is the only route in

resources.name: ASA Future Leaders of Amphibian Conservation
resources.description: Course fees, conference travel and project grants for early-career amphibian conservationists, with the amount varying by call. Applications open only when a call is running
resources.use_note: Watch for the next call, since it covers course fees and conference travel that most grants refuse

resources.name: Augustin-Pyramus de Candolle Prize
resources.description: CHF 5,000 every three years for the best monograph of a plant genus or family, and fungi and lichens count. Run by the Geneva Society of Physics and Natural History, with the conditions and each call's announcement on one stable page
resources.use_note: Read the current announcement on its page, which stays put between calls, before you prepare a submission

resources.name: Marsh Award for International Plant Conservation
resources.description: Plant conservation award run with Botanic Gardens Conservation International. Nominated through the BGCI network
resources.use_note: Get nominated through the BGCI network, so work with a botanic garden well beforehand

resources.name: Marsh Charitable Trust awards
resources.description: Thirty-plus awards, unusually dense in invertebrates and plants: entomology, four Lepidoptera awards, botany, marine and freshwater. Nomination only, and nominations go through the partner society for each award rather than to Marsh. No cash values published
resources.use_note: Scan all thirty for the invertebrate and plant awards, which are unusually well represented here

resources.name: David Fairchild Medal for Plant Exploration
resources.description: $5,000 every three years for plant exploration and rare plant conservation, awarded by nomination only. The two student awards on the same page do take direct applications, due January 15 and next in 2027
resources.use_note: Send students to the two awards on the same page, since the medal itself cannot be applied for

resources.name: GBIF Ebbe Nielsen Challenge
resources.description: €20,000 prize pool for tools built on GBIF-mediated data. Open submission with no nomination, and the call opens early in the year and closes late June
resources.use_note: Enter if you already built a tool on GBIF data, since the work is done

resources.name: Wildlife Photographer of the Year
resources.description: £10,000 to the grand title winner. You submit your own photographs, up to 25 for one entry fee, and the fee is waived for entrants aged 18 to 26 and for residents of more than a hundred listed countries and territories
resources.use_note: Check the fee waiver list first, since entrants aged 18 to 26 and residents of over a hundred listed countries enter free

resources.name: BigPicture: Natural World
resources.description: $5,000 grand prize plus category prizes, and exhibition at the California Academy of Sciences. You submit your own images, $25 for up to ten, and entries close in early March
resources.use_note: Enter by early March for a shot at exhibition, which is worth more than the cash

resources.name: Wildscreen Panda Awards
resources.description: Recognition rather than cash across 18 categories of conservation film and media, including a Digital-First category. You submit your own film, through FilmFreeway rather than to Wildscreen directly
resources.use_note: Enter a film in one of eighteen categories, including one for digital-first work

resources.name: Jackson Wild Media Awards
resources.description: Conservation film and media awards. Recognition rather than cash on the main awards, and you enter your own production when the annual call is open
resources.use_note: Enter for the recognition and the industry contact rather than for prize money

resources.name: BIOFIN
resources.description: UNDP biodiversity finance initiative, country plans and funding solutions
resources.use_note: Read your country's finance plan to see which mechanisms the government already backs

resources.name: RedLAC
resources.description: Network of environmental trust funds across Latin America and the Caribbean since 1999, with an annual conservation finance congress. In Spanish
resources.use_note: Approach the regional environmental fund covering your country, and attend the finance congress

resources.name: Cercarbono biodiversity certification protocol
resources.description: A working biodiversity credit standard with ten-year crediting periods, used mostly in Latin America
resources.use_note: Read an actual credit protocol before deciding whether biodiversity credits could fund your site

resources.name: TNC view on biodiversity credits
resources.description: Explainer separating biodiversity credits from offsets, for deciding whether to engage with credit markets at all
resources.use_note: Read it before a broker approaches you, so you can tell a credit from an offset

resources.name: IATI
resources.description: Open standard and tools for tracing international aid and humanitarian funding from funder to implementer, with ways to search the published data
resources.use_note: Trace which donors fund work in your country before you approach them

resources.name: Biodiversity Finance Trends
resources.description: Dashboard tracking international biodiversity finance flows against the finance targets of the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework
resources.use_note: Cite its trend figures in proposals and policy briefs to show the scale of the biodiversity finance gap

resources.name: Conservation Almanac
resources.description: Data and maps on public spending for land conservation across the United States, tracking money and acres by state and program
resources.use_note: Check what public programs have paid for land protection in your state to find the sources a purchase can draw on

resources.name: The Biodiversity Group
resources.description: Altruistic fiscal sponsorship for wildlife conservation nonprofits worldwide
resources.use_note: Apply for US tax-deductible status without incorporating, at the lowest affiliation fees we could find

resources.name: Multiplier
resources.description: Environmental fiscal sponsor hosting climate, ocean and conservation projects
resources.use_note: Apply on a rolling basis, with roughly six weeks from first inquiry to approval

resources.name: Re:wild Conservation Partners
resources.description: Hosts around 40 sponsored conservation programs, taking on legal and financial responsibility
resources.use_note: Approach if you want a well-known name carrying your legal and financial risk

resources.name: EarthShare
resources.description: Fiscal sponsor for environmental projects, requires most of the work to be conservation
resources.use_note: Check the conservation-share requirement first, since a mixed-mission project may not qualify at all

resources.name: The Ocean Foundation
resources.description: Marine conservation fiscal sponsor, accepts projects from anywhere in the world
resources.use_note: Apply from anywhere if the work is marine, which most US sponsors will not accept

resources.name: Windward Fund
resources.description: Environmental fiscal sponsor with a land and biodiversity portfolio
resources.use_note: Look here when the project is land or biodiversity rather than climate campaigning

resources.name: Wildlife Conservation Network
resources.description: Fiscal sponsorship for invited partner organizations, not open applications
resources.use_note: Do not apply, since partners are invited, but study who they pick and why

resources.name: Oregon Wildlife Foundation
resources.description: Fiscal sponsor for wildlife and habitat projects in Oregon
resources.use_note: Use it for Oregon work, where a local sponsor beats a national one on credibility

resources.name: Southern Conservation Partners
resources.description: Fiscal sponsor for land protection and habitat projects in the southern US
resources.use_note: Approach for land protection in the southern US, where regional knowledge matters most

resources.name: Earth Island Institute
resources.description: Long-running environmental fiscal sponsor, with a public directory of its projects
resources.use_note: Browse the project directory to see what a sponsored project looks like before becoming one

resources.name: Community Initiatives
resources.description: Large general-purpose fiscal sponsor, including environmental and animal projects
resources.use_note: Consider it when the project is not purely conservation, which narrower sponsors will refuse

resources.name: Tides
resources.description: Large fiscal sponsor and donor-advised platform
resources.use_note: Use it for scale and donor-advised infrastructure rather than for any conservation expertise

resources.name: Players Philanthropy Fund
resources.description: Low-cost fiscal sponsor for charitable projects of any cause, around 500 of them
resources.use_note: Compare its fees against the others, since low cost is the entire proposition

resources.name: TSNE
resources.description: Long-established sponsor offering the widest range of sponsorship models
resources.use_note: Ask which model they would use, because they offer more of them than anyone

resources.name: Panorama Global
resources.description: Global fiscal sponsor for social-impact and climate initiatives, 20+ countries
resources.use_note: Approach when a project spans several countries, which most US sponsors handle badly

resources.name: National Network of Fiscal Sponsors
resources.description: Directory of fiscal sponsors and the standards they sign up to
resources.use_note: Check whether a sponsor has signed the sector standards before you sign anything

resources.name: Fiscal Sponsor Directory
resources.description: Searchable directory of 420 sponsors across the US, Puerto Rico and Canada
resources.use_note: Search 420 sponsors by cause and state instead of guessing from a shortlist

resources.name: How to Find a Fiscal Sponsor
resources.description: Legal guide to choosing a sponsor, with a 15-point checklist for vetting one
resources.use_note: Work its fifteen-point checklist through a candidate sponsor before signing any agreement

resources.name: Fiscal Sponsorship: Six Ways To Do It Right
resources.description: The models explained by Gregory Colvin, who defined them
resources.use_note: Work out which of the six models you are being offered, since they differ enormously

resources.name: fiscalsponsorship.com
resources.description: Checklists, transfer guidelines and templates for sponsors and projects
resources.use_note: Take the templates and transfer guidelines, especially if you might change sponsors later

resources.name: Fiscal Sponsorship (Candid Learning)
resources.description: Plain-language introduction to how fiscal sponsorship works
resources.use_note: Send this to a board member who has never heard of fiscal sponsorship

resources.name: Human Nature Group
resources.description: Social science, strategy and evaluation consulting for mission-driven groups
resources.use_note: Hire them when a project needs social science rather than more ecology

resources.name: BLUeDNA Institute
resources.description: eDNA surveys, bioinformatics and protocol training for conservation programs
resources.use_note: Contract marine eDNA work end to end, or get your own protocols trained and checked

resources.name: Strategically Wild
resources.description: Species conservation strategy consulting
resources.use_note: Bring them in when a species needs a strategy and nobody internally has written one

resources.name: Global Conservation Solutions
resources.description: Conservation planning and facilitation services
resources.use_note: Hire for planning, coaching or geospatial work when you need it done rather than learned

resources.name: Maliasili
resources.description: Organizational development for local conservation groups
resources.use_note: Approach if you are a local group whose bottleneck is the organization, not the conservation

resources.name: Wildlife Impact
resources.description: Independent program evaluation and capacity development
resources.use_note: Commission an independent evaluation, which carries far more weight with funders than a self-report

resources.name: Conservation Strategy Fund
resources.description: Conservation economics analysis and training
resources.use_note: Get the economics done, or take their training so you can argue the value yourself

resources.name: IUCN SSC Conservation Planning Specialist Group
resources.description: Species planning workshops and mentoring
resources.use_note: Request a planning workshop when a species needs every range state in one room

resources.name: Capacity for Conservation
resources.description: Organizational health checks for conservation groups
resources.use_note: Run the free self-assessment before paying a consultant to tell you the same thing

resources.name: Development for Conservation
resources.description: Fundraising and board development consulting
resources.use_note: Bring them in when the board, not the program, is what limits your fundraising

resources.name: Conservation Careers coaching
resources.description: Career coaching and application review
resources.use_note: Get an application reviewed before sending it, which beats another year of rejections

resources.name: On Life and Wildlife grant writing
resources.description: Freelance conservation grant writing and editing
resources.use_note: Hire a freelance writer who already knows conservation vocabulary, so you edit far less

resources.name: Lupine Grant Strategies
resources.description: Grant writing for environmental nonprofits
resources.use_note: Ask for a grant readiness assessment first, since project-based pricing depends on it

resources.name: Conservation Coaches Network: Find a Coach
resources.description: Directory of conservation planning coaches you can bring into a project
resources.use_note: Search the coach database for someone near you rather than flying one in

resources.name: Conservation Finance Alliance professional services
resources.description: Directory of conservation finance consultants
resources.use_note: Find a finance consultant through members, which filters out those without a track record

resources.name: CIEEM Registered Practice Directory
resources.description: Searchable directory of ecological consultancies, UK and Ireland
resources.use_note: Check a UK or Irish consultancy is a registered practice before commissioning survey work

resources.name: Maine Land Trust Network consultants
resources.description: Regional directory of independent conservation consultants
resources.use_note: Find a Maine consultant for land trust work, where regional practice differs sharply

resources.name: Claude for Nonprofits
resources.description: Up to 75% off Team and Enterprise plans for 501(c)(3)s and international equivalents, with a free AI fluency course. Excludes government and higher education
resources.use_note: Apply for the discount and take the free fluency course before rolling anything out to staff

resources.name: Google Workspace for Nonprofits
resources.description: Free Workspace for eligible nonprofits up to 2,000 users, which is how Gemini and NotebookLM reach the sector at no cost. Paid tiers are discounted
resources.use_note: Get the free tier first, since it is how most small groups reach Gemini and NotebookLM

resources.name: OpenAI for Nonprofits
resources.description: ChatGPT Business at $8 per user per month on annual billing, and up to 75% off Enterprise through sales. The API is excluded
resources.use_note: Compare the per-seat price against real usage before switching a whole team over

resources.name: Microsoft for Nonprofits: AI
resources.description: Copilot Chat is included with any Microsoft 365 nonprofit subscription. Full Copilot is discounted, not free, and needs a paid base license on top
resources.use_note: Check what base license you already pay for, because Copilot needs one underneath it

resources.name: Grantable
resources.description: Drafts proposals from your own past submissions and prospects funders. Free tier, then $25 a month for nonprofits under $500k
resources.use_note: Draft from your own past proposals rather than a blank page, then check the fit scores

resources.name: One Hundred Nights
resources.description: AI consulting for nonprofits only, plus a free directory of 350+ reviewed AI tools if you would rather work it out yourself
resources.use_note: Use the free reviewed tool directory before paying anyone at all for AI advice

resources.name: NetHope Humanitarian AI Code of Conduct
resources.description: Thirteen principles for AI in humanitarian, development and conservation work, including a ban on synthetic imagery of program participants. Free
resources.use_note: Adopt it as your own AI policy, which is faster than drafting one from nothing

resources.name: Semantic Scholar
resources.description: Free literature search with AI-generated paper summaries and citation context, from the Allen Institute for AI, plus an open API if you want to build on it
resources.use_note: Search the literature free, and pull the API when you need citations at scale

resources.name: ResearchRabbit
resources.description: Give it a few papers you already trust and it builds a citation map outward from them, then keeps recommending. Free
resources.use_note: Start from three good papers and let it surface the ones your search terms missed

resources.name: Consensus
resources.description: Ask a research question and it answers from the literature, showing how much the papers agree rather than handing you one sentence. Free tier with capped searches
resources.use_note: Ask a question rather than guessing keywords, then check how much the papers actually agree

resources.name: Goodstack
resources.description: The eligibility check several vendors route nonprofit discounts through. Verify once here and it unlocks partner offers, usually in two or three days
resources.use_note: Verify once here and several vendor discounts unlock together, usually within a few days

resources.name: TechSoup
resources.description: Donated and discounted software from 100+ vendors once your nonprofit status is verified. Every product carries an admin fee, so compare against retail item by item
resources.use_note: Price each product against retail, because the admin fee sometimes exceeds the discount

resources.name: Connecting Up
resources.description: The Australian TechSoup partner, run by Infoxchange, which also operates TechSoup New Zealand at techsoup.net.nz
resources.use_note: Use this rather than TechSoup if you are based in Australia or New Zealand

resources.name: Google Ad Grants
resources.description: Up to $10,000 a month of free Google Search advertising, or $40,000 on GrantsPro. Needs 501(c)(3) status, a site you own with original mission content, Google Analytics, at least two ad groups per campaign and a click-through rate above 5%, or the account gets suspended. Government bodies, hospitals and schools excluded
resources.use_note: Audit your site content and Analytics before applying, since those are what actually fail accounts

resources.name: Salesforce Power of Us
resources.description: Ten free Salesforce licenses, one grant per EIN, and fiscally sponsored projects are accepted. Applied for through the Power of Us Portal. Several countries are excluded, so check before you plan around it
resources.use_note: Apply under one EIN, and confirm your country is eligible before designing around free licenses

resources.name: HubSpot for Nonprofits

resources.description: Free certifying courses on protected area management for rangers, researchers and managers, taught in French with some English. Finish them all and pass the exam and Senghor University of Alexandria awards an actual diploma
resources.use_note: Work through every MOOC and the exam if you want a credential, not just knowledge

resources.name: Google for Nonprofits AI training
resources.description: Three free short AI courses aimed at fundraising, creative work and workflows, plus a free AI usage policy builder
resources.use_note: Use the free policy builder to write an AI policy before staff start improvising

resources.name: IUCN Academy
resources.description: Free self-paced introductory courses in several languages including Arabic, French and Spanish, low-cost specialized courses, and paid hybrid professional certificates. Discounts for IUCN members and partial scholarships for nationals of least-developed and developing countries. Certificates are digital, not accredited
resources.use_note: Start with a free introductory course in your own language before paying for a certificate

resources.name: Top Conservation Skills
resources.description: What employers actually ask for, from an analysis of nearly 30,000 conservation job adverts across 100-plus countries. 41% of postings want communications skills, which is worth knowing before you plan any staff training
resources.use_note: Plan staff training around what postings actually demand, starting with communications

resources.name: Institute for Conservation Leadership
resources.description: Virtual workshops on running meetings that work, supporting a collaboration already underway, and emerging conservation topics. Facilitation and process skills rather than technical ones. Strict no-refund policy
resources.use_note: Book a facilitation workshop when the problem is the meeting rather than the ecology

resources.name: MPhil in Conservation Leadership, Cambridge
resources.description: A one-year cohort master's with a professional placement, not a short course. Placement partners have included Fauna & Flora. The most time-intensive option on this page, for a credentialed career pivot rather than a discrete skill
resources.use_note: Consider it only if you can stop working for a year, and study the placement partners

resources.name: Project Dragonfly
resources.description: Part-time 35-credit master's degrees from Miami University, finishable in two and a half to five years while working, based either at a partner US zoo or botanical garden or around international field expeditions. Shorter graduate certificates too
resources.use_note: Get a master's without relocating, based at a zoo or built around field expeditions

resources.name: Canva
resources.description: Design tool. Canva for Nonprofits gives eligible organizations the premium tier, including its AI design features, free for a team of up to 50
resources.use_note: Apply for the nonprofit tier before paying, then build templates your whole team reuses

resources.name: Piktochart
resources.description: Infographics
resources.use_note: Turn a results table into an infographic when a funder will not read the report

resources.name: Hemingway Editor
resources.description: Prose clarity
resources.use_note: Paste a grant paragraph in and cut until a non-specialist could read it

resources.name: BuzzSumo
resources.description: Content performance research
resources.use_note: Find which conservation stories already spread before pitching yours the same way

resources.name: HHMI BioInteractive
resources.description: Free biology teaching media
resources.use_note: Take free classroom-ready biology media instead of producing education content yourself

resources.name: Skype a Scientist
resources.description: Scientist and classroom matching
resources.use_note: Sign up as the scientist and reach classrooms without building an education program

resources.name: Roots & Shoots
resources.description: Youth program framework
resources.use_note: Adopt its framework when you want young people running projects rather than attending events

resources.name: Action for Conservation
resources.description: UK youth engagement
resources.use_note: Study its UK model for reaching teenagers who would never come to a nature reserve

resources.name: Photographers Without Borders
resources.description: Storytelling for NGOs
resources.use_note: Request ethical storytelling support when you need images but cannot pay a photographer

resources.name: iLCP ethical principles
resources.description: What the International League of Conservation Photographers holds its members to: welfare and conservation before the picture, and honesty about how the picture was made. The companion PDF works through the hard cases one at a time, including baiting, call playback, drone distance, chilling insects and captive animals in a documentary
resources.use_note: Adopt it as your own photography policy, and use the PDF to settle field arguments

resources.name: Our Better World
resources.description: Story platform
resources.use_note: Pitch a story when you want Asian audiences rather than Western donors

resources.name: Only One
resources.description: Ocean storytelling and action
resources.use_note: Use it to reach an ocean-focused audience already primed to act on something

resources.name: Mammalz
resources.description: Nature content platform
resources.use_note: Check the platform is still live before planning any content around it

resources.name: Hip Hop Science Show
resources.description: Science communication show
resources.use_note: Borrow the format when your audience is young and a lecture will not land

resources.name: BuzzHootRoar
resources.description: SciComm graphics
resources.use_note: Copy its one-graphic-per-idea format for explaining a finding on social media

resources.name: R Graph Gallery
resources.description: Chart references for R
resources.use_note: Find the chart type you need with the R code already written beside it

resources.name: Visualising Data
resources.description: Data visualization practice
resources.use_note: Read it before designing a figure, since most conservation charts fail on the basics

resources.name: NANPA ethical field practices
resources.description: The North American Nature Photography Association's principles for behaving well in the field and disclosing what you did afterwards
resources.use_note: Give it to volunteer photographers, especially the part about disclosing what you altered

resources.name: US Fish and Wildlife Service image library
resources.description: The agency calls this the premier source of public domain wildlife imagery, and it is the obvious first stop for a conservation organization. Free to reuse for any purpose; credit to the photographer and the Service is asked for, not required
resources.use_note: Start here for any US species photo, since nothing you take will need permission

resources.name: NOAA Fisheries photo gallery
resources.description: Public domain marine imagery by group: fish and sharks, corals and invertebrates, dolphins, sea turtles, seals. NOAA's National Ocean Service runs a separate coastal gallery at oceanservice.noaa.gov/gallery
resources.use_note: Search by species group when you need a free marine animal photograph

resources.name: USGS Multimedia Gallery
resources.description: Photos, video and audio across wildlife, landscapes, geology and water science. Public domain unless an item says otherwise, with the crediting format on the page
resources.use_note: Grab landscape, geology and water imagery, plus audio you can drop into a video

resources.name: NASA Image and Video Library
resources.description: Earth observation and Landsat imagery for habitat and land-cover context, not close-up wildlife: deforestation before and after, coastline change. Free with a source acknowledgement. The NASA insignia itself is protected separately
resources.use_note: Pull before-and-after satellite views to show habitat loss a ground photo cannot

resources.name: Ocean Image Bank
resources.description: Ocean and marine wildlife photography from The Ocean Agency, endorsed by the UN Ocean Decade and curated for conservation communication rather than incidentally licensed. Free for non-commercial use
resources.use_note: Use it for outreach rather than anything commercial, since the license stops there

resources.name: Wikimedia Commons wildlife photography
resources.description: Enormous community archive, but most of it is attribution and share-alike, so a crop for a banner has to carry the same license forward. Good for embedding with credit, awkward if you want to edit and rebrand
resources.use_note: Check the license on each image, because share-alike terms will follow your crop

resources.name: Flaticon
resources.description: Thousands of nature and conservation icons in SVG, PNG, EPS and icon-font formats. Free with attribution, paid to drop the credit line. The one to reach for when building an infographic or a threat-category key
resources.use_note: Build one consistent icon set for threats or habitats instead of mixing sources

resources.name: Google Fonts
resources.description: Web and desktop typefaces, most of them under the SIL Open Font License, free for commercial use with no attribution needed
resources.use_note: Pick two typefaces and stay with them, which is most of what a house style needs

resources.name: SIL Open Font License
resources.description: The license itself, from the nonprofit that wrote it. Worth reading once: it allows logos, books, apps and 3D prints freely and only forbids reselling the font files
resources.use_note: Read it once before putting a font in a logo, so you know what is permitted

resources.name: Unsplash
resources.description: General free stock photography with large wildlife and nature collections, no attribution required. Not vetted for conservation framing or species accuracy, so confirm what the animal actually is before you caption it
resources.use_note: Use it for mood and landscape shots, never where a species must be identified

resources.name: Pexels
resources.description: Free stock photos and video, commercial use allowed, no attribution required. Same caveat as Unsplash on species accuracy
resources.use_note: Search here when you need video rather than stills and have no budget

resources.name: Pixabay
resources.description: Free stock photos, video, illustrations and vectors under a blanket permissive license. Useful as a fallback when a specific species or region is not in the government galleries
resources.use_note: Try it when a specific region or species is missing from the government galleries

resources.name: Species Black List rediscoveries
resources.description: Species turning up again after years unrecorded, checked daily across fourteen national news editions
resources.use_note: Scan what the press is claiming about a rediscovery before you cite it as confirmed

resources.name: Reverse the Red
resources.description: IUCN SSC movement for species recovery. You can make a Species Pledge or apply for an Accelerator Award
resources.use_note: Make a Species Pledge, or apply for an Accelerator Award to fund a recovery step

resources.name: Conservation Optimism
resources.description: Seven stories of optimism every week, plus a positive communication toolkit, a podcast and regional hubs in Ghana, India, Pakistan and the UK
resources.use_note: Send the weekly stories to a tired team, and take the communication toolkit

resources.name: Mongabay conservation solutions
resources.description: 4,155 stories on what actually worked, with an RSS feed you can pipe into a newsletter
resources.use_note: Pipe the RSS feed into your own newsletter instead of curating good news by hand

resources.name: Reasons to be Cheerful
resources.description: Nonprofit solutions journalism with a climate and environment section, publishing several times a week
resources.use_note: Pitch a solutions story here when the outcome, not the crisis, is the news

resources.name: Positive News
resources.description: Environment section with a conservation subcategory, covering rewilding and species recovery
resources.use_note: Point supporters at recovery coverage when the usual news cycle is grinding them down

resources.name: Squirrel News
resources.description: Free nonprofit app and newsletter, thirty constructive stories a week curated from other outlets
resources.use_note: Install the free app and get thirty constructive stories a week without searching

resources.name: Mongabay
resources.description: Conservation news, including a conservation-tech series
resources.use_note: Read the conservation-tech series, and pitch them when you have a story worth reporting

resources.name: ConservationBytes
resources.description: Research blog, Corey Bradshaw
resources.use_note: Read it for blunt argument about conservation science rather than institutional messaging

resources.name: IUCN Crossroads
resources.description: IUCN opinion blog
resources.use_note: Watch which controversies IUCN members are actually willing to air in public

resources.name: Conservation Visions
resources.description: Wild harvest initiative
resources.use_note: Read the Wild Harvest Initiative when you need the hunting and harvest side of an argument

resources.name: James Borrell
resources.description: Fieldwork and careers writing
resources.use_note: Send early-career staff his career writing instead of repeating the same advice yourself

resources.name: The Revelator
resources.description: Editorially independent conservation journalism, Center for Biological Diversity
resources.use_note: Read it for reporting that stays independent of the organization funding it

resources.name: Anthropocene Magazine
resources.description: Weekly digest of sustainability and conservation science
resources.use_note: Subscribe to keep up with sustainability science without reading the journals yourself

resources.name: The Weekly Anthropocene
resources.description: Climate and biodiversity news roundup, Sam Matey
resources.use_note: Get a weekly biodiversity and climate roundup written for people who need hope

resources.name: The Xylom
resources.description: Weekly newsletter on health, climate and environmental disparity
resources.use_note: Subscribe when you want the environmental justice framing most conservation media leaves out

resources.name: Nature's Archive
resources.description: Ecology and natural history interviews, Michael Hawk
resources.use_note: Listen for natural history depth, and note that it is now part of Jumpstart Nature

resources.name: In Defense of Plants
resources.description: Botany and plant conservation interviews and field stories
resources.use_note: Send it to anyone who thinks plants are the boring part of a survey

resources.name: Sounds Wild
resources.description: Endangered species podcast, Center for Biological Diversity
resources.use_note: Use episodes as background briefing on a listed species before a meeting

resources.name: WCS Wild Audio
resources.description: Field reporting from Wildlife Conservation Society projects
resources.use_note: Hear how a large organization tells a field story, useful when you write your own

resources.name: BatChat
resources.description: Bat ecology podcast, UK Bat Conservation Trust
resources.use_note: Catch UK bat survey practice and licensing talk that never reaches a journal

resources.name: Rewilding the World
resources.description: Interviews on rewilding and nature recovery, Ben Goldsmith
resources.use_note: Listen for how rewilding projects were actually financed, not just how they were designed

resources.name: Species Unite
resources.description: Weekly conversations on animal rights and wildlife protection
resources.use_note: Listen when you need the animal rights perspective on a conservation decision

resources.name: Our Wild Lives
resources.description: Stories from wildlife professionals in the field, The Wildlife Society
resources.use_note: Play an episode to a student who wants to know what the job is really like

resources.name: Conservation Careers Podcast
resources.description: Interviews on building a career in conservation
resources.use_note: Listen for how people entered the field, which beats any job description

resources.name: Future of Conservation
resources.description: Conservation science and history series, US Fish and Wildlife Service
resources.use_note: Get the US agency view on conservation history, useful before any federal conversation
